answer: As of FY2022, Boeing shows a modestly improving GAAP gross margin profile, with gross profit increasing from $3,017 million (4.84% of revenue) in FY2021 to $3,502 million (5.26% of revenue) in FY2022. However, due to the long-term, complex nature of its contracts, Boeing relies heavily on program accounting and estimates of margins at completion over the life of multi-year production programs, rather than simple point-of-sale gross margins.
rationale: Boeing's GAAP gross profit and revenues were obtained from reported facts, yielding a gross margin of 4.84% in 2021 and 5.26% in 2022. Program accounting details from Item 7 explain why gross margin metrics are evaluated in the context of long-term program estimates.

citations.quote: Program accounting requires the demonstrated ability to reliably estimate revenues, costs and gross profit margin for the defined program accounting quantity.
